intent: A size people misjudge: the camera visits each island as it is named, the to-scale bars make the winner 3 times the runner-up, a flash marks the ice sheet fact, and the population counter stops at a number smaller than a town.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which is the LARGEST island on Earth?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which is the largest island on Earth?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Greenland. Over 2 million square kilometres of island.

lines.direction: hold the island wide; the to-scale area bars rise on 'Borneo' — three bars, the winner towering; a jungle sticker on 'Borneo', a lemur sticker on 'Madagascar'; a muscle sticker on 'Greenland' as the island pulses
lines.text: Borneo is huge, and Madagascar is bigger than France. Greenland is almost 3 times bigger than either.

lines.direction: push north over the ice; a white flash and the 80% ICE card on 'percent'; a snowflake on 'ice'; a ruler sticker on 'thick' as the island pulses
lines.text: About 80 percent of it is buried under a single ice sheet, which in places is up to 3 kilometres thick.

lines.direction: push south-west to the coast; the island rises with a people sticker on it on 'people' and the 56,000 card lands; the Nuuk pin and tag land on 'Nuuk' with a house sticker as the island pulses; pin leaves
lines.text: Only around 56,000 people live on the whole island, most of them along the south west coast, around the small capital, Nuuk.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
